claim: EBA-175 has a well-defined role in binding to glycophorin A (GpA) during Plasmodium falciparum invasion of erythrocytes.
source: Erythrocyte Binding Antigen of 175 kDa (EBA-175) has a well-defined role in binding to glycophorin A (GpA) during Plasmodium falciparum invasion of erythrocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations in the text (Orlandi et al., 1990; Orlandi et al., 1992; Klotz et al., 1992; Sim et al., 1994; Salinas and Tolia, 2014a; Liang and Sim, 1997; Sim, 1998; Duraisingh et al., 2003; Tolia et al., 2005; Wanaguru et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2014b) and is presented as established knowledge.

claim: EBA-175 is shed post invasion.
source: However, EBA-175 is shed post invasion and a role for this shed protein has not been defined.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation (O'Donnell et al., 2006) mentioned later in the text and is presented as established knowledge.

claim: EBA-175 shed from parasites promotes clustering of RBCs.
source: We show that EBA-175 shed from parasites promotes clustering of RBCs, and EBA-175-dependent clusters occur in parasite culture.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Region II of EBA-175 is sufficient for clustering RBCs in a GpA-dependent manner.
source: Region II of EBA-175 is sufficient for clustering RBCs in a GpA-dependent manner.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2, demonstrating that RII alone can induce clustering.

claim: EBA-175-mediated RBC clusters are capable of forming under physiological flow conditions.
source: These clusters are capable of forming under physiological flow conditions and across a range of concentrations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from flow assays presented in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: EBA-175-dependent RBC clustering provides daughter merozoites ready access to uninfected RBCs enhancing parasite growth.
source: EBA-175-dependent RBC clustering provides daughter merozoites ready access to uninfected RBCs enhancing parasite growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing growth enhancement in Figure 3 and microscopy images in Figure 3D.

claim: RBC clustering provides protection from neutralizing antibodies that target AMA-1 and RH5.
source: Clustering provides a general method to protect the invasion machinery from immune recognition and disruption as exemplified by protection from neutralizing antibodies that target AMA-1 and RH5.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4 showing reduced antibody neutralization in the presence of RII-mediated clustering.

claim: Plasmodium falciparum is a causative agent of malaria that alternates between an insect vector and a human host.
source: Plasmodium falciparum is a causative agent of malaria that alternates between an insect vector and a human host.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the malaria parasite life cycle.

claim: During the erythrocytic cycle, merozoite stage parasites invade red blood cells (RBCs) to initiate asexual replication.
source: During the erythrocytic cycle, merozoite stage parasites invade red blood cells (RBCs) to initiate asexual replication.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the malaria parasite life cycle.

claim: Invasion of RBCs by parasites is a multistage process characterized by 1) initial weak engagement of the RBC by the parasite, 2) apical reorientation of the parasite and strong anchoring to the RBC, 3) tight junction formation, 4) active invasion utilizing an actin-myosin motor, and 5) shedding of the surface proteins of the parasite.
source: Invasion of RBCs by parasites is a multistage process characterized by 1) initial weak engagement of the RBC by the parasite, 2) apical reorientation of the parasite and strong anchoring to the RBC, 3) tight junction formation, 4) active invasion utilizing an actin-myosin motor, and 5) shedding of the surface proteins of the parasite (Cowman et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cowman et al., 2017 and represents established knowledge about parasite invasion.

claim: EBA-175 binds to the host receptor glycophorin A (GpA) and this interaction has a well-defined role in anchoring the parasite during invasion of erythrocytes.
source: Erythrocyte Binding Antigen of 175 kDa (EBA-175) is a P. falciparum protein that binds to the host receptor glycophorin A (GpA) and this interaction has a well-defined role in anchoring the parasite during invasion of erythrocytes (Orlandi et al., 1990; Orlandi et al., 1992; Klotz et al., 1992; Sim et al., 1994; Salinas and Tolia, 2014a; Liang and Sim, 1997; Sim, 1998; Duraisingh et al., 2003; Tolia et al., 2005; Wanaguru et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations and represents established knowledge.

claim: EBA-175 modifies the cellular and biophysical nature of the RBC cytoskeletal complex in preparation for efficient invasion by the parasite.
source: EBA-175 has also been shown to modify the cellular and biophysical nature of the RBC cytoskeletal complex in preparation for efficient invasion by the parasite (Koch et al., 2017; Sisquella et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Koch et al., 2017 and Sisquella et al., 2017.

claim: During invasion, the tight junction formed in part by EBA-175 and GpA moves from the apical end to the posterior end of the merozoite.
source: During invasion, the tight junction formed in part by EBA-175 and GpA moves from the apical end to the posterior end of the merozoite and EBA-175 is shed from the surface of the parasite into the surrounding media during the last steps of invasion (O'Donnell et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to O'Donnell et al., 2006 and represents established knowledge.

claim: EBA-175 is shed from the surface of the parasite into the surrounding media during the last steps of invasion.
source: During invasion, the tight junction formed in part by EBA-175 and GpA moves from the apical end to the posterior end of the merozoite and EBA-175 is shed from the surface of the parasite into the surrounding media during the last steps of invasion (O'Donnell et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to O'Donnell et al., 2006.

claim: EBA-175 is a member of the Erythrocyte Binding like (EBL) family of Plasmodium proteins that includes DBP, EBL-1, EBA-140, and EBA-181.
source: EBA-175 is a member of the Erythrocyte Binding like (EBL) family of Plasmodium proteins that includes DBP, EBL-1, EBA-140, and EBA-181 (Miller et al., 1975; Adams et al., 1992; Lobo et al., 2003; Maier et al., 2009; Batchelor et al., 2011; Lin et al., 2012; Malpede et al., 2013; Batchelor et al., 2014; Malpede and Tolia, 2014; Paing and Tolia, 2014; Salinas and Tolia, 2016; Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations and represents established knowledge about protein families.

claim: DBL domains are targets for structural vaccinology.
source: EBL family members bind host-cell receptors via minimal binding domains comprised of either a single or double Duffy-binding like (DBL) domain (Sim et al., 1994; Salinas and Tolia, 2014a; Liang and Sim, 1997; Duraisingh et al., 2003; Tolia et al., 2005; Wanaguru et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2014b; Adams et al., 1992; Lobo et al., 2003; Maier et al., 2009; Batchelor et al., 2011; Lin et al., 2012; Malpede et al., 2013; Batchelor et al., 2014; Malpede and Tolia, 2014; Paing and Tolia, 2014), and these domains are targets for structural vaccinology (Chen et al., 2013; Batchelor et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2013; Batchelor et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016.

claim: The minimal binding domain of EBA-175, region II (RII), is comprised of two DBL domains, F1 and F2.
source: The minimal binding domain of EBA-175, region II (RII), is comprised of two DBL domains, F1 and F2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), which together bind to GpA to form a tight junction between the parasite and RBC in the initial stages of invasion (Sim et al., 1994; Salinas and Tolia, 2014a; Tolia et al., 2005; Salinas et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing the domain structure.

claim: F1 and F2 together bind to GpA to form a tight junction between the parasite and RBC in the initial stages of invasion.
source: The minimal binding domain of EBA-175, region II (RII), is comprised of two DBL domains, F1 and F2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), which together bind to GpA to form a tight junction between the parasite and RBC in the initial stages of invasion (Sim et al., 1994; Salinas and Tolia, 2014a; Tolia et al., 2005; Salinas et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Binding of GpA induces EBA-175 dimerization to facilitate high avidity associations.
source: Binding of GpA induces EBA-175 dimerization to facilitate high avidity associations (Salinas and Tolia, 2014a; Tolia et al., 2005; Wanaguru et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2014b; Paing and Tolia, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: EBA-175 binding to GpA is dependent on the terminal sialic acid residues of O-linked glycans on the extracellular domain of GpA.
source: This binding is dependent on the terminal sialic acid residues of O-linked glycans on the extracellular domain of GpA (Orlandi et al., 1992; Sim et al., 1994; Salinas and Tolia, 2014a; Wanaguru et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Removal of sialic acid by neuraminidase or specific mutation of O-linked glycans ablates binding both in direct protein:protein interactions and in parasite culture.
source: Removal of sialic acid by neuraminidase or specific mutation of O-linked glycans ablates binding both in direct protein:protein interactions and in parasite culture (Salinas et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Salinas et al., 2014b.

claim: Specific O-linked glycans on GpA allow for the specificity of EBA-175 for GpA over its highly related family member glycophorin B.
source: These specific O-linked glycans on GpA also allow for the specificity of EBA-175 for GpA over its highly related family member glycophorin B (Salinas et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Salinas et al., 2014b.

claim: Antibodies to invasion proteins are known to prevent invasion and reduce parasite growth.
source: Many of these proteins are involved in establishing a tight junction during invasion and antibodies to these proteins are known to prevent invasion and reduce parasite growth.
evidence: This is established knowledge about antibody function against malaria parasites.

claim: The interaction between EBA-175 and GpA can be blocked by antibodies that target the dimer interface and glycan binding pockets of EBA-175.
source: The interaction with GpA can be blocked by antibodies (Abs) that target the dimer interface and glycan binding pockets of EBA-175 (Chen et al., 2013; Ambroggio et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2013 and Ambroggio et al., 2013.

claim: Ab-217, a mouse monoclonal that targets the dimer interface and glycan binding pockets of EBA-175, has an IC50 of 0.1 mg/mL for parasites and can block binding of EBA-175 to GpA.
source: Ab-217, a mouse monoclonal that targets these regions, has an IC50 of 0.1 mg/mL for parasites and can block binding of EBA-175 to GpA (Chen et al., 2013; Sim et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2013 and Sim et al., 2011.

claim: Ab-218, a mouse monoclonal that targets a non-functional epitope in EBA-175, does not block the EBA-175-GpA interaction and has minimal effects on parasite viability.
source: Ab-218, another mouse monoclonal that targets a non-functional epitope in EBA-175, does not block this interaction and has minimal effects on parasite viability (Chen et al., 2013; Sim et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2013 and Sim et al., 2011.

claim: RH5, a member of the RH family, binds to the RBC receptor basigin, which is essential for invasion.
source: RH5, a member of the RH family, binds to the RBC receptor basigin, which is essential for invasion (Crosnier et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Crosnier et al., 2011.

claim: AMA1 binds to a parasite protein RON2, which is inserted into the RBC plasma membrane; this interaction is crucial for the active invasion of RBCs by the parasite.
source: Post-attachment, another parasite protein, AMA1, binds to a parasite protein RON2, which is inserted into the RBC plasma membrane; this interaction is crucial for the active invasion of RBCs by the parasite (Vulliez-Le Normand et al., 2012; Srinivasan et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Vulliez-Le Normand et al., 2012 and Srinivasan et al., 2011.

claim: Both RH5 and AMA1 are promising vaccine candidates for malaria and are targets of neutralizing Abs.
source: Both RH5 and AMA1 are promising vaccine candidates for malaria and are targets of neutralizing Abs (Douglas et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Douglas et al., 2014.

claim: Purified endogenously shed EBA-175 promotes RBC clustering.
source: We demonstrate that purified endogenously shed EBA-175 promotes RBC clustering and that recombinant soluble RII domain of EBA-175 is sufficient to promote RBC clustering in a GpA-dependent manner.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Recombinant soluble RII domain of EBA-175 is sufficient to promote RBC clustering in a GpA-dependent manner.
source: We demonstrate that purified endogenously shed EBA-175 promotes RBC clustering and that recombinant soluble RII domain of EBA-175 is sufficient to promote RBC clustering in a GpA-dependent manner.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: RII-mediated red cell clustering enhances parasite growth by providing daughter merozoites ready access to uninfected RBCs.
source: This RII-mediated red cell clustering enhances parasite growth by providing daughter merozoites ready access to uninfected RBCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: RII-mediated RBC clustering confers protection from neutralizing Abs that target diverse heterologous invasion proteins.
source: Furthermore, we demonstrate that RII-mediated RBC clustering confers protection from neutralizing Abs that target diverse heterologous invasion proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: A soluble, not a membrane-anchored, parasite protein can promote clustering of RBCs which may contribute to malaria pathogenesis by enhancing parasite growth and facilitating immune evasion.
source: This study highlights that a soluble, not a membrane-anchored, parasite protein can promote clustering of RBCs which may contribute to malaria pathogenesis by enhancing parasite growth and facilitating immune evasion.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented throughout the study.

claim: Over two hundred million new cases of malaria are reported worldwide annually with an estimated half a million deaths.
source: Over two hundred million new cases of malaria are reported worldwide annually with an estimated half a million deaths.
evidence: This is established epidemiological knowledge about malaria.

claim: The majority of malaria deaths are due to severe malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum parasites.
source: The majority of these deaths are due to severe malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum parasites.
evidence: This is established epidemiological knowledge about malaria.

claim: EBA-175-mediated clustering may facilitate the high parasite burdens observed during severe malaria.
source: EBA-175-mediated clustering may facilitate the high parasite burdens observed during severe malaria, protect parasites from antibody recognition, and prevent infected erythrocyte clearance.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the findings of the study.

claim: EBA-175-mediated clustering may protect parasites from antibody recognition.
source: EBA-175-mediated clustering may facilitate the high parasite burdens observed during severe malaria, protect parasites from antibody recognition, and prevent infected erythrocyte clearance.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the findings of the study, though supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: EBA-175-mediated clustering may prevent infected erythrocyte clearance.
source: EBA-175-mediated clustering may facilitate the high parasite burdens observed during severe malaria, protect parasites from antibody recognition, and prevent infected erythrocyte clearance.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the findings of the study.

claim: Native EBA-175 was purified from a culture of Dd2 schizonts that had undergone rupture and reinvasion overnight.
source: Upon rupture of Dd2 schizonts and reinvasion overnight, the culture medium was harvested, concentrated 40x by centrifugation using 10 kDa molecular mass cutoff concentrators (MilliporeSigma).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: Purified native EBA-175 was observed on a Coomassie stained protein gel as a band at ~175 kDa in the anti-EBA-175 lane.
source: Purified native EBA-175 was observed on a Coomassie stained protein gel as a band at ~175 kDa in the anti-EBA-175 lane (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The control pulldown using a non-specific antibody, Ab-8C2, did not result in a similar band pattern to the EBA-175 pulldown.
source: The control pulldown using a non-specific antibody, Ab-8C2, did not result in a similar band pattern.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Immunoblot analysis of IP elutions with an α-EBA175 specific antibody detected a band at 175 kDa in α-EBA175 IP lane but none in control lane.
source: Immunoblot analysis of these IP elutions with an α-EBA175 specific antibody detected a band at 175 kDa in α-EBA175 IP lane but none in control lane that (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The most abundant peptides identified in the α-EBA175 pulldown corresponded to EBA-175 while no EBA-175 specific peptide was detected in the control pulldown.
source: The most abundant peptides identified in the α-EBA175 pulldown corresponded to EBA-175 while no EBA-175 specific peptide was detected in the control pulldown (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D.

claim: Peptides identified in the α-EBA175 pulldown were dispersed throughout the ectodomain of EBA-175 indicating the full-length shed protein was captured.
source: Peptides identified were dispersed throughout the ectodomain of EBA-175 indicating the full-length shed protein was captured (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Native EBA-175 induced clustering of RBCs while the control elution showed no size change.
source: The native EBA-175 induced clustering of RBCs while the control elution showed no size change (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The frequency of clusters for the native EBA-175 sample was noticeably higher than that of the control sample.
source: The frequency of clusters for the native sample was noticeably higher than that of the control sample (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E) indicating native EBA-175 promotes clustering of RBCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Clustering was dependent on the concentration of EBA-175 as purifications that resulted in increased yields of EBA-175 resulted in higher levels of clustering.
source: Clustering was dependent on the concentration of EBA-175 as purifications that resulted in increased yields of EBA-175 resulted in higher levels of clustering (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: A large FSC-A signal was seen in the untreated NF54-GFP-Luc cultures at high parasitemia.
source: A large FSC-A signal was seen in the untreated NF54-GFP-Luc cultures.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The cultures in the presence of Ab-217 contained significantly fewer clusters in the gated population compared to untreated cultures.
source: The cultures in the presence of Ab-217 contained significantly fewer clusters in the gated population (Figure 1E bottom panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: All samples showed high levels of GFP demonstrating the Ab treatments had no effect on parasite invasion.
source: All samples showed high levels of GFP demonstrating the Ab treatments had no effect on parasite invasion (Figure 1E top panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: A large portion of the higher size particles seen in parasite culture are clusters dependent on EBA-175 binding to RBCs in a GpA-dependent manner.
source: Overall, these data suggest that a large portion of the higher size particles seen are clusters dependent on EBA-175 binding to RBCs in a GpA-dependent manner.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing Ab-217 blocking of clusters.

claim: Incubation of RBCs with picomolar and low nanomolar concentrations of RII resulted in RBC clustering by confocal live imaging of RBCs.
source: Incubation of RBCs with picomolar and low nanomolar concentrations of RII resulted in RBC clustering by confocal live imaging of RBCs (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: RBC clustering by RII could be seen as low as 300 pM of RII.
source: This RBC clustering could be seen as low as 300 pM of RII.
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The picomolar and low nanomolar concentrations indicate EBA-175 RII has a potent effect in inducing RBC clustering.
source: The picomolar and low nanomolar concentrations indicate EBA-175 RII has a potent effect in inducing RBC clustering.
evidence: This is an inference based on the low concentrations required for clustering.

claim: RII-mediated clustering effect was observed in multiple blood types tested.
source: Furthermore, this clustering effect was observed in multiple blood types tested (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: RII, but not the individual DBL domains F1 or F2, induces RBC clustering in a concentration dependent manner.
source: RII, but not the individual DBL domains F1 or F2, induces RBC clustering in a concentration dependent manner as observed by FSC-A.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Incubation of RBCs with various concentrations of RII resulted in a concentration-dependent change in particle size as characterized by an increase in forward scatter.
source: Incubation of RBCs with various concentrations of RII resulted in a concentration-dependent change in particle size as characterized by an increase in forward scatter.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: F1 and F2 were unable to facilitate RBC clustering even at very high concentrations tested.
source: In contrast, F1 and F2 were unable to facilitate RBC clustering even at very high concentrations tested.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The full RII domain is necessary to facilitate clustering of RBCs consistent with prior studies that demonstrate both DBL domains are required for RBC binding.
source: This indicates that the full RII domain is necessary to facilitate clustering of RBCs consistent with prior studies that demonstrate both DBL domains are required for RBC binding (Salinas and Tolia, 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citation to Salinas and Tolia, 2014a.

claim: The lack of red cell clustering in the presence of F1 or F2 indicates that the clustering effect is specific to RII and not solely due to the addition of DBL domains to the media.
source: The lack of red cell clustering in the presence of F1 or F2 also indicates that the clustering effect is specific to RII and not solely due to the addition of DBL domains to the media.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing F1 and F2 do not cause clustering.

claim: Confocal live imaging of RBCs incubated with RII revealed that the increased particle size corresponded to multiple RBCs adhering to one another to form clusters.
source: Confocal live imaging of RBCs incubated with RII revealed that the increased particle size corresponded to multiple RBCs adhering to one another to form clusters (Figure 2A & C).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2A & C.

claim: Fluorescent Ab labeling showed that RII-6XHis-tag localized to the edges of the RBCs and was strongest in the junctions between adjacent RBCs.
source: Fluorescent Ab labeling showed that RII-6XHis-tag localized to the edges of the RBCs and was strongest in the junctions between adjacent RBCs (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: RII localization to the edges of RBCs and junctions between adjacent RBCs implies that RII mediates the adherence of the RBCs.
source: This localization implies that RII mediates the adherence of the RBCs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the localization data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Neuraminidase treatment of RBCs prevented RII mediated red cell clustering.
source: Neuraminidase treatment of RBCs removes the terminal sialic acid residues of GpA necessary for EBA-175 binding (Orlandi et al., 1992; Salinas et al., 2014b) and abolished RII mediated red cell clustering (Figure 2D panel 2), indicating that the binding of sialic acid residues in GpA by EBA-175 is a prerequisite for red cell clustering.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The binding of sialic acid residues in GpA by EBA-175 is a prerequisite for red cell clustering.
source: Neuraminidase treatment of RBCs removes the terminal sialic acid residues of GpA necessary for EBA-175 binding (Orlandi et al., 1992; Salinas et al., 2014b) and abolished RII mediated red cell clustering (Figure 2D panel 2), indicating that the binding of sialic acid residues in GpA by EBA-175 is a prerequisite for red cell clustering.
evidence: This is an inference based on the neuraminidase treatment data.

claim: The α-GpA Ab prevents EBA-175 access to GpA and abolished RBC clustering.
source: The α-GpA Ab prevents EBA-175 access to GpA (Salinas and Tolia, 2014a), and also abolished RBC clustering (Figure 2D panel 3,4) demonstrating the requirement of EBA-175 binding to the RBC receptor.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2D and citation.

claim: Ab-217 binds to the dimer interface and the glycan binding pocket of RII to specifically disrupt EBA-175 binding to GpA.
source: Ab-217 binds to the dimer interface and the glycan binding pocket of RII to specifically disrupt EBA-175 binding to GpA (Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2013.

claim: Ab-217 prevented red cell clustering.
source: Again, Ab-217 prevented red cell clustering (Figure 2D panel 5,6).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The RII mediated clustering of RBCs is dependent on GpA interacting with EBA-175.
source: Taken together, these data show that the RII mediated clustering of RBCs is dependent on GpA interacting with EBA-175.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing various blocking agents prevent clustering.

claim: RBC clusters were observed at all concentrations of EBA-175 RII tested (1, 10, and 100 nM) under 1 dyn/cm2 shear stress.
source: Clusters were observed at all concentrations tested and the mean cluster area (1 nM - 289.7 ± 207.8; 10 nM – 223.4 ± 60.7 and 100 nM – 1135.3 ± 360.1), and mean number of clusters (1 nM – 21.3 ± 6.1; 10 nM – 88.6 ± 15.6 and 100 nM – 233.0 ± 32.4), increased in response to protein concentration (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow assay data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The mean cluster area and mean number of clusters increased in response to EBA-175 RII protein concentration under flow conditions.
source: Clusters were observed at all concentrations tested and the mean cluster area (1 nM - 289.7 ± 207.8; 10 nM – 223.4 ± 60.7 and 100 nM – 1135.3 ± 360.1), and mean number of clusters (1 nM – 21.3 ± 6.1; 10 nM – 88.6 ± 15.6 and 100 nM – 233.0 ± 32.4), increased in response to protein concentration (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow assay data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Pre-incubation of RBCs with EBA-175 RII generated clusters capable of withstanding 1 dyn/cm2, with no clusters observed in the untreated control.
source: The pre-incubation of RBC's with EBA-175 RII generated clusters capable of withstanding 1 dyn/cm2, with no clusters observed in the untreated control.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow assay data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: As the concentration of EBA-175 RII increased, the number of free RBCs was reduced, with almost all RBCs contained within clusters at 100 nM.
source: As the concentration increased, the number of free RBCs was reduced, with the most striking effect observed at the highest concentration tested (100 nM), where almost all RBCs were contained within clusters, with very few remaining free (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Data generated from physiological flow assays illustrate the adhesive strength of the EBA-175 RII protein.
source: These data generated from physiological flow assays illustrate the adhesive strength of the EBA-175 RII protein.
evidence: This is an inference based on the flow assay data.

claim: A significant increase in parasite growth was observed when RII was present at concentrations as low as 300 pM (p<0.05, in Dd2 strain).
source: A significant increase in parasite growth was observed when RII was present at concentrations as low as 300 pM (p<0.05, in Dd2 strain) and could be seen up to 10 nM (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The significant growth enhancement at 1 nM RII (p<0.001) was also observed in a NF54 line expressing a firefly luciferase transgene, NF54-GFP-luc.
source: The significant growth enhancement at 1 nM, p<0.001, was also observed in a NF54 line expressing a firefly luciferase transgene, NF54-GFP-luc (Figure 3A panel 5), demonstrating that the growth enhancement phenotype was not due to non-specific effects of RII on [3H]-hypoxanthine incorporation into parasite nucleic acids.
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The growth enhancement phenotype was not due to non-specific effects of RII on [3H]-hypoxanthine incorporation into parasite nucleic acids.
source: The significant growth enhancement at 1 nM, p<0.001, was also observed in a NF54 line expressing a firefly luciferase transgene, NF54-GFP-luc (Figure 3A panel 5), demonstrating that the growth enhancement phenotype was not due to non-specific effects of RII on [3H]-hypoxanthine incorporation into parasite nucleic acids.
evidence: This is an inference based on the luciferase assay data confirming the hypoxanthine assay results.

claim: The growth enhancement effect was observed in multiple blood types tested.
source: Further, the growth enhancement effect was observed in multiple blood types tested (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A significant increase in parasite growth was observed when RII was present at concentrations from 10 nM to 100 nM with an optimal concentration of 30 nM.
source: A significant increase in parasite growth was observed when RII was present at concentrations from 10 nM to 100 nM with an optimal concentration of 30 nM (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: F1 was unable to promote parasite growth.
source: Assessment of F1 and F2 revealed that F1 was unable to promote growth, while F2 evidenced moderate growth promoting activity at concentrations higher than 100 nM (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1) consistent with high avidity binding of EBA-175 to GpA requiring both DBL domains (Salinas and Tolia, 2014a; Tolia et al., 2005; Wanaguru et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: F2 evidenced moderate growth promoting activity at concentrations higher than 100 nM.
source: Assessment of F1 and F2 revealed that F1 was unable to promote growth, while F2 evidenced moderate growth promoting activity at concentrations higher than 100 nM (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1) consistent with high avidity binding of EBA-175 to GpA requiring both DBL domains (Salinas and Tolia, 2014a; Tolia et al., 2005; Wanaguru et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 3B and is consistent with citations.

claim: The observed growth enhancement in parasite culture requires an intact RII with both DBL domains.
source: Therefore, the observed growth enhancement in parasite culture requires an intact RII with both DBL domains.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing F1 and F2 alone are insufficient.

claim: Ab-217 blocked the RII-mediated growth enhancement.
source: Ab-217 blocked the RII-mediated growth enhancement (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) while the Ab-DBP had no effect on growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 3C and supplementary figures.

claim: Ab-DBP had no effect on RII-mediated growth enhancement.
source: Ab-217 blocked the RII-mediated growth enhancement (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) while the Ab-DBP had no effect on growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The concentrations of Ab-217 used were far below the IC50 on invasion and did not cause any effects on invasion.
source: The concentrations of Ab-217 used were far below the IC50 on invasion (Sim et al., 2011) and did not cause any effects on invasion.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and the experimental design.

claim: EBA-175 promotes RBC clustering in a GpA-dependent manner which results in a higher growth of parasite culture, due to the increase in invasion into adjacent adherent uninfected RBCs.
source: Taken together, the data suggest that EBA-175 promotes RBC clustering in a GpA-dependent manner which results in a higher growth of parasite culture, due to the increase in invasion into adjacent adherent uninfected RBCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data from clustering and growth assays.

claim: Microscopy analysis of NF54-GFP-luc cultures in the presence of nanomolar RII revealed large clusters of uninfected RBCs associated with infected RBCs.
source: Microscopy analysis of NF54-GFP-luc cultures in the presence of nanomolar RII revealed large clusters of uninfected RBCs associated with infected RBCs (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: More than one parasite was observed in the clusters and these tend to group together in adjacent RBCs.
source: More than one parasite was observed in the clusters and these tend to group together in adjacent RBCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Multiple daughter merozoites, arising from a single schizont, invade adjacent uninfected RBCs within a cluster.
source: This suggests that multiple daughter merozoites, arising from a single schizont, invade adjacent uninfected RBCs within a cluster.
evidence: This is an inference based on the microscopy observations.

claim: Red cell clustering may provide daughter merozoites ready access to uninfected RBCs by bringing the uninfected RBCs in close proximity to egressing merozoites.
source: Therefore, red cell clustering may provide daughter merozoites ready access to uninfected RBCs by bringing the uninfected RBCs in close proximity to egressing merozoites.
evidence: This is an inference based on the microscopy observations and growth data.

claim: The two α-AMA1 antibodies (N3-2D9 and N4-1F6) blocked the growth of 3D7 parasites by 20% and 50%, respectively in the absence of RII.
source: The two α-AMA1 antibodies blocked the growth of 3D7 parasites by 20% and 50%, respectively in the absence of RII.
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Addition of 30 nM RII strongly reduced the ability of α-AMA1 antibodies to neutralize 3D7 parasites.
source: Strikingly, addition of 30 nM RII strongly reduced the ability of these Abs to neutralize parasites (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The FVO-FCR1 parasites are more sensitive to AMA-1 Abs with 25% and 65% inhibition by N3-2D9 and N4-1F6, respectively.
source: The FVO-FCR1 parasites are more sensitive to AMA-1 Abs with 25% and 65% inhibition by N3-2D9 and N4-1F6, respectively (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The inhibitory effect of AMA-1 neutralizing Abs on FVO-FCR1 was significantly mitigated in the presence of 30 nM RII.
source: As in 3D7, this inhibitory effect of AMA-1 neutralizing Abs on FVO-FCR1 was also significantly mitigated in the presence of 30 nM RII (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The protection from neutralizing Abs was not due to artifacts of the hypoxanthine incorporation assay as a similar elimination of Ab neutralization was observed in NF54-GFP-luc parasites measured using luciferase activity.
source: The protection from neutralizing Abs was not due to artifacts of the hypoxanthine incorporation assay as a similar elimination of Ab neutralization was observed in NF54-GFP-luc parasites measured using luciferase activity (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 9AD4 exhibited dose-dependent inhibition with maximal inhibition of 80% observed at 1 mg/mL of Ab concentration for 3D7, FVO/FCR1, and Dd2 in the absence of RII.
source: In our assays, 9AD4 exhibited dose-dependent inhibition with maximal inhibition of 80% observed at 1 mg/mL of Ab concentration for 3D7, FVO/FCR1, and Dd2 in the absence of RII (Figure 4D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 4D–F.

claim: 30 nM RII was able to protect against inhibition by 9AD4 in the parasite lines 3D7, FVO/FCR1, and Dd2 at all concentrations tested.
source: Strikingly, and similar to the results seen with the α-AMA1 Abs, 30 nM RII was able to protect against inhibition by 9AD4 in the parasite lines 3D7, FVO/FCR1, and Dd2 at all concentrations tested (Figure 4D–F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 4D–F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: RII-mediated RBC clustering can protect parasites from neutralizing Abs that target diverse heterologous antigens, providing a mechanism for immune evasion.
source: These results demonstrate that RII-mediated RBC clustering can protect parasites from neutralizing Abs that target diverse heterologous antigens, providing a mechanism for immune evasion.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing protection from multiple antibodies.

claim: Shed EBA-175 facilitates formation of RBC clusters to benefit parasite growth and survival.
source: The results support a model (Figure 5) in which shed EBA-175, perhaps in conjunction with other membrane-anchored proteins, facilitates formation of RBC clusters to benefit parasite growth and survival.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental findings.

claim: During infection, EBA-175 on the surface of parasites interacts with GpA on the surface of RBCs during invasion.
source: During infection, EBA-175 on the surface of parasites interacts with GpA on the surface of RBCs during invasion (Sim et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Post invasion, EBA-175 is released into the surrounding environment where it binds to uninfected RBCs, facilitating EBA-175- and GpA-dependent clustering of naïve RBCs around the infected RBCs.
source: Post invasion, we and others (O'Donnell et al., 2006) have shown that EBA-175 is released into the surrounding environment where it binds to uninfected RBCs, facilitating EBA-175- and GpA-dependent clustering of naïve RBCs around the infected RBCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from this study and citation to O'Donnell et al., 2006.

claim: Red cell clustering confers protection from antibodies and the immune system, promoting efficient invasion of adjacent uninfected RBCs by daughter merozoites.
source: Red cell clustering subsequently confers protection from antibodies and the immune system, promoting efficient invasion of adjacent uninfected RBCs by daughter merozoites.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing immune protection and growth enhancement.

claim: The enhancement of invasion into adjacent uninfected RBCs leads to an increase in parasite growth and the process perpetuates through the next round of uninfected RBC recruitment.
source: The enhancement of invasion into adjacent uninfected RBCs leads to an increase in parasite growth and the process perpetuates through the next round of uninfected RBC recruitment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and proposed model.

claim: Red cell clustering and growth enhancement were observed at picomolar concentrations of EBA-175 implying that this phenomenon could exist in vivo.
source: We observed red cell clustering and growth enhancement at picomolar concentrations of EBA-175 implying that this phenomenon could exist in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the low concentrations required for the observed effects.

claim: Picomolar concentrations of EBA-175 are likely achievable during malaria infection particularly in the capillaries and extremities of blood vessels.
source: These concentrations are likely achievable during malaria infection particularly in the capillaries and extremities of blood vessels.
evidence: This is speculation based on the low concentrations required and knowledge of parasite biology.

claim: EBA-175-mediated clustering may be a mechanism, along with rosetting afforded by membrane-anchored proteins, for the high parasitemia seen in severe malaria through enhancement of parasite growth and immune evasion.
source: This may be a mechanism, along with rosetting afforded by membrane-anchored proteins, for the high parasitemia seen in severe malaria through enhancement of parasite growth and immune evasion.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental findings.

claim: The mechanism described is direct evidence for active immune evasion by Plasmodium parasites.
source: This mechanism is also direct evidence for active immune evasion by Plasmodium parasites and offers new insights into parasite-host interactions and vaccine development.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing protection from neutralizing antibodies.

claim: This phenomenon may be relevant for the interpretation of the data generated from EBA-175-based vaccines in clinical trials.
source: This phenomenon may be relevant for the interpretation of the data generated from EBA-175-based vaccines in clinical trials.
evidence: This is speculation about the implications of the findings.

claim: The model proposed is consistent with synergistic inhibition observed when α-EBA-175 and α-RH5 antibodies are used in combination.
source: The model proposed is consistent with synergistic inhibition (Ord et al., 2012; Williams et al., 2012) observed when α-EBA-175 and α-RH5 antibodies are used in combination.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ord et al., 2012 and Williams et al., 2012.

claim: The synergistic inhibition arises as EBA-175 red cell clustering is prevented, allowing for increased inhibition by α-RH5 Abs.
source: The model indicates that the synergistic inhibition arises as EBA-175 red cell clustering is prevented, allowing for increased inhibition by α-RH5 Abs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the proposed model and experimental data.

claim: The clustering phenomenon reported here exhibits similarities to P. falciparum rosetting attributed to the parasite membrane proteins PfEMP1, RIFINs and STEVORs.
source: The clustering phenomenon reported here exhibits similarities to P. falciparum rosetting attributed to the parasite membrane proteins PfEMP1 (Rowe et al., 1997; Moll et al., 2015; Chen et al., 1998), RIFINs (Goel et al., 2015) and STEVORs (Niang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on rosetting proteins.

claim: PfEMP-1 is related to the EBL family as it contains multiple DBL domains including the DBLα domain which binds to the RBC receptor CR1 during sequestration of rosettes.
source: PfEMP-1 is related to the EBL family as it contains multiple DBL domains including the DBLα domain which binds to the RBC receptor CR1 during sequestration of rosettes (Rowe et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Rowe et al., 1997.

claim: RIFINs bind to blood group A RBCs to form rosettes.
source: RIFINs bind to blood group A RBCs to form rosettes (Goel et al., 2015) and may bind to GpA on RBCs to mediate rosetting (Goel et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Goel et al., 2015.

claim: RIFINs may bind to GpA on RBCs to mediate rosetting.
source: RIFINs bind to blood group A RBCs to form rosettes (Goel et al., 2015) and may bind to GpA on RBCs to mediate rosetting (Goel et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Goel et al., 2015.

claim: STEVORs bind to RBCs through glycophorin C.
source: STEVORs bind to RBCs through glycophorin C (Niang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Niang et al., 2014.

claim: Evidence of growth enhancement and immune protection from Abs due to rosetting has yet to be reported.
source: However, evidence of growth enhancement and immune protection from Abs due to rosetting has yet to be reported.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Both PfEMP1 and RIFINs appear to prefer type A blood for rosetting and show minimal binding to type O blood.
source: It is also important to note that both PfEMP1 and RIFINs appear to prefer type A blood for rosetting and show minimal binding to type O blood (Goel et al., 2015; Vigan-Womas et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Goel et al., 2015 and Vigan-Womas et al., 2012.

claim: Red cell clustering defined here is independent of blood type and provides a novel pathway for RBC clustering that complements PfEMP1, RIFINs or STEVORs.
source: Red cell clustering defined here is independent of blood type and provides a novel pathway for RBC clustering that complements PfEMP1, RIFINs or STEVORs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing clustering in multiple blood types.

claim: Individuals in regions endemic for malaria develop partial immunity to all parasite invasion ligands and yet incidences of severe malaria still occur.
source: Individuals in regions endemic for malaria develop partial immunity to all parasite invasion ligands and yet incidences of severe malaria still occur.
evidence: This is established knowledge about malaria immunity.

claim: EBA-175-mediated enhancement of growth may simply outpace the ability of the immune system to target parasites and prevent invasion.
source: The first mechanism is that EBA-175-mediated enhancement of growth simply outpaces the ability of the immune system to target parasites and prevent invasion.
evidence: This is speculation about possible mechanisms based on the findings.

claim: RBC clustering may limit the time window of antigen exposure to neutralizing antibodies during the rapid invasion of an adjacent RBC, preventing Ab access.
source: The second is that RBC clustering limits the time window of antigen exposure to neutralizing antibodies during the rapid invasion of an adjacent RBC, preventing Ab access.
evidence: This is speculation about possible mechanisms based on the findings.

claim: RBC clustering may block physical access of the antibodies to parasites during invasion.
source: The third is that RBC clustering may block physical access of the antibodies to parasites during invasion.
evidence: This is speculation about possible mechanisms based on the findings.

claim: The three proposed mechanisms for immune evasion are not mutually exclusive and the true mechanism may be a combination of the three.
source: These mechanisms are not mutually exclusive and the true mechanism may be a combination of the three.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanisms.
